Office Visit - Follow-up
Patient: Rosa Zielinski | DOB: 08/13/1987 | MRN: SYN-3073567
Date of service: 01/31/2025 | Dr. Isla Kestrel, MD

History of present illness:
37-year-old woman seen for follow-up of low back pain. She first noticed the pain shooting down her right leg after a weekend of gardening, nearly four months before this visit.

Treatment to date:
Two months of supervised exercise sessions plus over-the-counter anti-inflammatories have not brought lasting relief.

History:
Past medical history: hypothyroidism, type 2 diabetes.
Medications: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; metformin 500 mg twice daily.

Spine Consultation
Patient: Rosa Zielinski | DOB: 08/13/1987 | MRN: SYN-3073567
Date of service: 01/31/2025 | Dr. Kaveh Kestrel, DO

Reason for consultation:
Low back pain with right leg symptoms, referred by Dr. Isla Kestrel, MD.

Review of systems:
No trouble controlling urine or stool, no numbness in the groin area, no fevers, stable weight, and no prior malignancy.

Physical exam:
Back: tenderness over the lower lumbar paraspinal muscles; straight-leg raise positive on the right at 30 degrees.
She cannot rise onto her toes on the right as well as on the other side, the ankle jerk is reduced on the right, and touch feels dull along the outer edge of that foot.

Assessment and plan:
Assessment: right S1 lumbar radiculopathy.
Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to evaluate for disc herniation; home exercise program; follow up after imaging.
